# References to mine — auditing-deployment-and-trust-boundaries

## From category #45

### Key references

- **OWASP — Top 10 CI/CD Security Risks** — https://owasp.org/www-project-top-10-ci-cd-security-risks/ (originated as Cider Security's research, donated to OWASP) → mine: **Poisoned Pipeline Execution (PPE)** — a pipeline that executes attacker-influenced content from the very branch/artifact it just fetched, with no intervening trust gate — names exactly the git-sync-then-execute shape #191 reports. Also **Insufficient Credential Hygiene** (a deploy identity's blast radius exceeding what it deploys) and **Insufficient PBAC** (pipeline-based access control: is a job's *reach* proportional to what triggering it *requires*). *(verify exact `CICD-SEC-N` numbering — the risk names and definitions are well-established, the current numbering scheme less so.)*
- **SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), OpenSSF** — https://slsa.dev/ → mine: **build provenance** as the countermeasure to PPE — a deploy step should be able to state *what it is running and where that came from*, not merely "the current contents of a directory." Useful vocabulary (`source`/`build`/`provenance` tracks) even where a repo is nowhere near a formal SLSA level.
- **GitHub — "Security hardening for GitHub Actions"** — https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions → mine: `pull_request_target` combined with a checkout of the PR's own head is the canonical PPE instance in GitHub Actions (the workflow runs with base-repo secrets/permissions but on attacker-supplied code); pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, not a mutable tag; prefer OIDC short-lived credentials over long-lived deployment secrets.
- **MITRE ATT&CK** — cross-reference to #38's own citation rather than re-cited here; useful the same way for grounding "what can go wrong" in a concrete attacker technique once a suspect boundary is found.
- **#14/#31/#19/#30/#32 boundary — see G1 note below.** #45 names a threat in the deployment/execution wiring and **delegates** the deep verdict the same way #38 does; it never re-runs those lenses' own checklists.
